items.name: Stacked words
items.summary: Giant words stacked to fill the frame, each one as wide as the frame.
items.use: For a run of two to four words that sum something up, on the beat of the music: a process, a promise, a rallying cry. Full bleed, in the brand; short words work best, in capitals.
items.motion: Each word slams in on the beat, top to bottom (0.18 s, a hard ease out, from 130%), then the accent band lands behind the last one, wiping in from the left (0.30 s). Each word is sized to run the full width. Out: the words drop away and fade, top to bottom (0.30 s).

fields.label: The words, top to bottom, separated by | (two to four)

items.name: Footage in letters
items.summary: Footage plays inside one giant word.
items.use: For a bold title moment: a word that fills the frame, with the video showing through its letters. Full bleed on the brand's background, which needs to be a light colour; one short word reads best.
items.motion: The word sets in solid, rising 30 px (0.40 s, the brand ease), then the footage fades up inside the letters (0.50 s) and keeps playing. Out: the word fades (0.40 s).

fields.label: The footage that plays inside the letters (video file)

items.name: Ticker
items.summary: A band of words scrolls steadily across the frame.
items.use: For a run of things to show at once without reading each: services, features, places, names. Full screen, in the brand; short items work best, and the line loops for as long as the scene runs.
items.motion: The band wipes in from the left (0.40 s, the brand ease), then the line scrolls right to left at a steady 160 px a second, looping, with a square in the accent between items. Out: the band wipes away to the right (0.30 s).

fields.label: Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Split reveal
items.summary: A line sets on, then the frame splits open along it to reveal the next scene.
items.use: To move into a new scene on a line that introduces it: a how-to, a demo, the next chapter. Put it on a track above the next scene; the frame splits along the line and the scene behind shows through.
items.motion: The line rises 30 px and fades in (0.40 s, the brand ease) on a full-frame background, and holds. Then the frame splits just under it: the top half lifts away with the line and the bottom half drops (0.70 s, easing in and out), revealing the next scene behind.

fields.label: The line the frame splits along
When the frame splits open (seconds in)

items.name: Zoom through
items.summary: The camera flies into a big word, through the hole in its O, into the next scene.
items.use: To move into a new scene with energy, on a word with an O in it. Put it on a track above the next scene: the camera flies through the O and the scene behind fills the frame.
items.motion: The word sets on in the middle of the frame (0.30 s). Then the camera pushes into it and through the middle of the O (1.00 s, easing in), and the next scene behind fills the frame as it passes.

fields.label: The word (it needs an O to fly through)
When the camera pushes in (seconds in)

items.name: Repeat
items.summary: A word repeats down a dark screen, each brighter, the last in the accent.
items.use: For a word to drive home: an instruction, a value, a mantra. On the brand's dark colour, since an accent like yellow is too faint as text on a light one; a short word or two reads best.
items.motion: The word repeats down the screen a line at a time (0.08 s apart), each rising 20 px and fading up brighter than the one above (0.25 s), and the last lands in the accent with a small bump in size. The caption fades up after it. Out: the lines fade and lift away (0.30 s).

fields.label: Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: List build
items.summary: A numbered list builds, each new line pushing the others up.
items.use: For steps, reasons or points the voiceover counts through. Full screen, in the brand; keep each line short, and set the gap to the voiceover's pace.
items.motion: Each new line slides up from the bottom (0.40 s, easing out) and pushes the list up a line; the older lines fade back to 35%, so the newest always reads first. The caption fades up after the last. Out: the list lifts away and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The list, in order, separated by | (two to five short lines)
fields.default: Pick a goal.|Make a plan.|Take the first step.

fields.label: Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Roll
items.summary: Lines roll up the screen like closing credits.
items.use: For the end of a video: who presented it, who made it, the music, where to find out more. On the brand's dark colour; each credit is a small role over a name.
items.motion: The credits roll up at a steady pace (about 60 px a second), fading in at the bottom of the frame and out at the top. The caption fades up and stays. Out: the last credits keep rolling as everything fades (0.40 s).

fields.label: The credits, each as Role: Name, separated by |
fields.default: Presented by: Jordan Lee|Produced by: Your company|Edit and motion: Sam Rivera|Music: Track name, Artist|Thanks for watching: yourwebsite.com

fields.label: Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Question and answer
items.summary: A question types on, then the answer drops into its place.
items.use: For a question people ask and its short answer: a frequently asked question, a myth, a quiz. Full screen, in the brand; keep the answer to a few words.
items.motion: The question types on (about 18 characters a second) and holds a beat, then lifts, softens and fades as the answer drops into its place (0.40 s, easing out). The caption fades up after it. Out: the answer and caption fade and lift away (0.30 s).

fields.label: The question
fields.default: How long does it take to set up?

fields.label: Characters a second, as the question types
Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Name line
items.summary: A name and role set in type over the footage, without a card.
items.use: To introduce someone on screen, lighter than a lower third. There's no card behind it, so place it on a calm, darker part of the frame.
items.motion: The name rises out of a mask (0.45 s, easing out), then the role types on beneath it (0.30 s) after its square pops in. It holds, then both drop back into their masks (0.30 s).

items.name: Callouts
items.summary: Lines point from small labels to things in the footage.
items.use: For naming what's on screen: a person, a part of a product, a tool, a place in the shot. Up to four labels; give the pixel point each one marks, and the side its label sits.
items.motion: Each dot pops on its point (0.15 s), the line draws out to its label (0.30 s) and the label wipes in (0.20 s). The callouts follow 0.25 s apart. Out: everything fades (0.25 s).

fields.label: The labels, separated by | (up to four)
What each points at, as x,y in pixels from the top left, separated by | (leave empty for the stand-in)
Which side of its point each label sits, left or right, separated by |

items.name: Handle
items.summary: A social handle with its platform's icon, low in the frame.
items.use: When the presenter tells people where to find them: one handle on one platform. Pick the platform for its icon; the pill sits low on the side away from the presenter.
items.motion: The pill rises in (0.30 s), the icon pops in (0.20 s, a slight overshoot), then the handle types on beside it (about 20 characters a second). It holds, then slides down out of the frame (0.30 s).

items.name: Location
items.summary: A place and date type on, documentary style.
items.use: To set the scene at the start of a shot: where and when it was filmed. Low in the frame on a calm part of the footage; it cuts out with the shot.
items.motion: The place types on behind a block cursor (about 14 characters a second), then the date follows on the line below, the cursor moving with it and blinking (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off) once it's typed. It holds, then cuts out with the shot.

fields.label: The date or time (leave empty for none)

items.name: Price reveal
items.summary: The old price is struck through, then the new price types on, big.
items.use: For an offer or a price drop: what it was and what it is now. Full screen, in the brand; the prices here are a neutral example.
items.motion: The old price rises 20 px and fades in, and the strike draws through it (0.30 s, the brand ease). Then the new price types on behind a blinking caret, a character at a time, and the caret blinks (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off) as it holds. The caption fades up after it. Out: the prices and caption fade and lift away (0.30 s).

fields.label: The old price (leave empty for none)
Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Hashtag
items.summary: A campaign hashtag builds letter by letter behind a caret.
items.use: For a campaign or event hashtag people should remember and use. Full screen, in the brand; the letters still to come wait faintly, so the tag's shape shows from the start.
items.motion: The # fades up, then the hashtag builds a letter at a time (about 12 a second) behind a caret in the accent, the letters still to come waiting at 10%. Then the caret blinks twice and fades. The caption fades up after it. Out: the hashtag and caption fade and lift away (0.30 s).

fields.label: Caption line, as Label · words (leave empty for none)

items.name: Mini chart
items.summary: A trend at a glance, when a full chart would stop the story.
items.use: When the presenter mentions how something has grown or fallen over time, and the shape of the line says it. Up to a dozen points, the latest figure large, and always the source. The chart starts at zero.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The baseline draws left to right (0.60 s), the line follows (1.60 s), then the last point turns to the accent as the figure counts up (1.00 s). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The latest figure (it counts up to this; keep any % or commas)
The figures over time, oldest first, separated by commas
Label at the start of the line
Label at the end of the line
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Do and don't
items.summary: The right way and the wrong way, in two lines.
items.use: When the presenter contrasts a good habit with a common mistake. Keep each to a short line, and bring the wrong way in as it's said.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The right way builds first: its mark scales in, the tick draws and the words fade up. The wrong way follows 0.40 s later (or on its cue), its cross drawing as two strokes (0.15 s each). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The right way
fields.default: Read your script aloud before you record

fields.label: When the wrong way comes in (seconds; 0: just after the right way)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Definition
items.summary: A term the viewer might not know, explained in one sentence.
items.use: The first time the presenter uses a word of the trade, so nobody gets left behind. One term, one plain sentence; the note underneath is optional.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The term types on, about 20 letters a second, then the meaning fades up 12 px (0.40 s) and the note follows 0.20 s later. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What it means, in one sentence
fields.default: A sketch of every scene, in order, so you can see your video before it’s animated.

fields.label: A short note underneath (optional)
fields.default: You approve it before animation begins

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Tip
items.summary: An aside or a piece of advice.
items.use: When the presenter shares a tip worth remembering, or an aside that would break the flow if said in full. Two or three short sentences at most.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The rail draws down (0.90 s), the marker scales in at its top (0.35 s), then the eyebrow and the tip fade up a line at a time (0.10 s apart). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The tip
fields.default: Write for the ear, not the eye. Read your script aloud and cut anything you stumble over.

fields.label: Size: 1 reads on a phone, up to 2 for more (it grows from its own side)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Rating
items.summary: Stars and a claim, for social proof.
items.use: While a client or the presenter talks about results. Use the real rating and say where it comes from.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The stars pop in left to right (0.20 s each, 0.06 s apart), then the claim and where it comes from fade up. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Fact sheet
items.summary: A few facts at once, set like a title block.
items.use: When the presenter introduces a company, a product or a project with a few headline figures. Two to four figures, each with a short label.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its top line. The grid lines draw (0.60 s), then each figure counts up, left to right, 0.15 s apart (1.00 s each, easing out). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What each figure is, separated by | (two to four)
The figures, in the same order (they count up; keep any +, % or commas)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Link
items.summary: Point viewers to a page, report or tool.
items.use: When the presenter mentions somewhere to go next: a guide, a report, a sign-up page. Keep the address short enough to read and remember.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s), the eyebrow and title 0.10 s apart. Then the address types on, about 30 letters a second, and the arrow nudges right twice (6 px, 0.30 s). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Chapter marker
items.summary: A small slate in the corner as a section starts.
items.use: At the start of each section of a longer video, so viewers know where they are. Pair it with the step names in W01 Process tracker.
items.motion: The marker scales in, the chip wipes open from it (0.40 s) and the words type on. It holds, then the chip wipes back into the marker, which goes.

items.name: Before and after
items.summary: Two numbers and the change between them.
items.use: When the presenter talks about a change: last year and this, before and after a fix, us and the average. Say what changed on the chip, and give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The before figure fades up, muted (0.30 s), the arrow draws left to right (0.60 s), then the after figure counts up from the before value (1.00 s, easing out) and the change chip pops in (0.25 s). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: After (it counts up from the before figure)
The change, on the accent chip
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Progress ring
items.summary: A percentage as a ring that fills, or a thermometer, a battery or a glass.
items.use: When the presenter gives a share of something: how many people, how much of a goal. The ring suits most figures; the thermometer suits a target or a fundraiser, the battery energy or capacity, and the glass something filling up. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The ring's empty track draws round from the top (0.60 s), or the thermometer, battery or glass draws on (0.40 s). Then it fills to the figure (1.20 s, easing out) as the number counts up with it; the glass's surface keeps rolling gently. The words and source fade up as it settles. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The percentage (it fills to this and counts up)
What it is
fields.default: of customers use the app every week

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Donut chart
items.summary: Shares of a whole, up to five parts.
items.use: When the presenter splits a whole into a few parts: where customers come from, how a budget is spent. Two to five parts, largest first, with the one being talked about in the accent and its figure in the middle. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The parts draw round clockwise from the top in one sweep (1.20 s), each legend row fading up as its part lands, then the figure in the middle counts up (0.80 s, easing out). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The parts, separated by | (two to five)
Their shares, in the same order (keep any %)
The part in the accent, its figure in the middle (1 is the first)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Comparison bars
items.summary: Two or three bars side by side, such as us and them.
items.use: When the presenter compares two or three figures: us and the average, this channel and that one. The bars start at zero and the tallest is the largest figure; put the one being talked about in the accent, and always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The baseline draws left to right (0.40 s), then the bars grow up from it, 0.15 s apart (0.80 s each, easing out), each figure counting up as its bar rises. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: Eyebrow (what it compares)
fields.default: How customers prefer to get help

fields.label: What each bar is, separated by | (two or three)
Their figures, in the same order (they count up; keep any % or commas)
The bar in the accent (1 is the first)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Ranking
items.summary: A top five, with bars, highest first.
items.use: When the presenter runs through a top five (or a top three): the most used, the most asked for. List them highest first. Build it top first to show the whole picture, or fifth to first when the top spot is the reveal. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The rows fade up top to bottom, 0.10 s apart, then each bar grows from the left (0.70 s, easing out) as its figure counts up. As a reveal, the rows build from fifth to first instead, 0.45 s apart, each bar growing as its row arrives. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The names, highest first, separated by | (two to five)
fields.default: Offline mode|Shared folders|Dark theme|Calendar sync|Bulk export

fields.label: Their figures, in the same order (they count up; keep any % or commas)

options.label: Fifth to first, as a reveal

fields.label: The row in the accent (1 is the top)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Timeline
items.summary: Milestones along a line, by year or date.
items.use: When the presenter tells a short history or a plan: where it started, where it is now, what comes next. Two to four milestones, each a year or date and a few words. When the last is still to come, the line to it is dashed.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The markers pop in left to right, 0.30 s apart, the line drawing between them, and each milestone’s words fade up as its marker lands. The last marker fills with the accent. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: Each milestone’s year or date, separated by | (two to four)
What happened at each, in the same order
fields.default: Founded in a spare room|12,000 customers in 30 countries|A new app, this spring

options.label: Still to come (a dashed line to it)

items.name: Gauge
items.summary: A value on a dial from low to high.
items.use: When the presenter gives a score or a level that reads as high or low: satisfaction, a rating, how far to a goal. The dial runs from zero to its top (100 for a percentage). Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The dial draws left to right (0.60 s), then the needle swings up from zero with the fill (1.20 s, easing out with a small overshoot) as the figure counts up. The words and source fade up as it settles. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The figure (the needle swings to it as it counts up; keep any %)
What it is
fields.default: of customers would recommend us to a friend

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Price card
items.summary: A plan, its price and what’s included.
items.use: When the presenter gives a price: a plan, an offer, a launch price. The price large, what it’s per beside it, and up to five things it includes. Use the tag for the plan you want people to pick.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The plan fades up and the tag pops in (0.25 s), the price counts up from 0 (0.80 s, easing out), then the included rows tick in, 0.30 s apart. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The price (it counts up from 0; keep the currency sign)
What’s included, separated by | (up to five)
fields.default: Unlimited projects|Review links for clients|Priority support

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Countdown
items.summary: Days or hours left, for a launch or an offer.
items.use: When the presenter mentions a deadline: an offer ending, a launch, an event. Two to four tiles, largest unit first (days, hours, minutes, seconds). With the last tile counting down, it should be seconds.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The tiles flip in left to right (0.30 s each, 0.08 s apart). While it holds, the last tile flips down once a second like a split-flap (0.25 s), and the one before it flips as the seconds roll over. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: Time left, largest unit first, separated by | (two to four)
The units, in the same order

options.label: The last tile counts down each second

fields.label: Under the tiles (leave empty for none)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Map pin
items.summary: A place on a small map, with one detail.
items.use: When the presenter mentions where something is: an office, an event, a store, where a story happened. The map is an illustration, not a real map of the place; the words say where it is.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) as the map fades in and drifts 2% closer over the hold. The pin drops in with a small bounce (0.35 s), a ring pulses out from it twice (0.80 s each) and a dashed ring settles round it, turning slowly. Then the label, place and details fade up. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: Label by the pin (leave empty for none)
Under it
fields.default: Opening in the spring, by the river

items.name: Versus
items.summary: Two options head to head, row by row.
items.use: When the presenter weighs two options against each other on a few measures: two plans, two channels, before and after. One to four rows; the bars grow out from the middle, so the longer side wins each row at a glance. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The names slide in from their own sides (0.40 s) and the VS pops (0.25 s). Then each row's bars grow out from the centre line together (0.70 s, easing out) as the figures count up, rows 0.30 s apart. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The first option (left, in the accent)
What each row compares, separated by | (one to four)
The first option’s figures, in the same order (keep any %)
The second option’s figures, in the same order

items.name: Sum
items.summary: A quick calculation: its inputs and the answer.
items.use: When the presenter works something out: what a small change is worth, what a saving adds up to. Two figures, the sum between them, and the answer, each with a few words. Check the answer: the widget shows the one you give it.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The two figures build top to bottom, 0.40 s apart, each counting up (0.60 s). The rule draws left to right (0.40 s), then the answer counts up (0.80 s, easing out) as the accent wipes in behind it. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The first figure (it counts up; keep any %, £ or commas)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Score
items.summary: A score on a scale, such as 8 out of 10.
items.use: When the presenter gives a verdict as a score: a review, a rating out of ten, how something measures up. Up to 20 steps show as they are; a longer scale (out of 100) shows as ten steps. Keep the verdict to a sentence.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s) with its eyebrow. The steps fill with the accent left to right, 0.06 s apart (0.20 s each), as the score counts up to match. The verdict fades up once the count settles. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The score (it counts up; it can have a decimal)
The verdict, in a sentence
fields.default: Most teams are up and running in a day.

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Testimonial
items.summary: A customer’s words, with their name, role and photo.
items.use: When a customer's words make the point better than the presenter can. Keep the quote to two or three sentences, use a real customer with their permission, and hold it for about twice the time it takes to read.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The quote mark scales in (0.30 s), the words fade up a line at a time (0.10 s apart), then the photo and name slide in from the left (0.40 s). Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What they said
fields.default: Since we switched, onboarding a new client takes half the time. The whole team noticed in the first week.

fields.label: Their photo (image file in the project; leave empty for their initials)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Review
items.summary: A star rating with the review and the reviewer.
items.use: When a review backs up what the presenter says: a rating from a review site, an app store or a customer survey. Quote it as written, with the reviewer, and hold it for about twice the time it takes to read.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The stars pop in left to right (0.20 s each, 0.06 s apart) as the score counts up. The review fades up a line at a time (0.10 s apart), then the reviewer row. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The review

fields.label: Beside the reviewer (leave empty for none)

fields.default: Saw the advert|Visited the site|Signed up

items.name: Poll
items.summary: A question and how people answered, like a social poll.
items.use: When the presenter shares how people answered a question: a survey, a social poll, a vote. Two to four answers; the one most people chose is ticked. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The question fades up, then the answers fade in as empty bars, 0.10 s apart. They fill together from the left (1.00 s, easing out) while the percentages count up; the winner fills with the accent and its tick pops in (0.30 s). The votes and source fade up as it settles. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: The question
fields.default: Which delivery option would you use most?

fields.label: The answers, separated by | (two to four)
fields.default: A weekend slot|An evening slot, 6–9pm|A pick-up point near me|A parcel locker

fields.label: How many chose each, in the same order (keep any %)
Under the answers (leave empty for none)
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Balance
items.summary: Two amounts weighed, such as cost and return.
items.use: When the presenter weighs one amount against another: cost and return, effort and reward, before and after. The heavier side tips down, so put the one that wins on the right. Always give the source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The scale draws on, level (0.40 s). The left amount drops onto its pan and the beam dips left (0.40 s), then the right one drops onto its pan a weight at a time (0.15 s apart) and the beam tips its way with a damped wobble (0.80 s). The amounts count up as they land; the words and source fade up as it settles. Out: the content fades (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: Its amount (it counts up; keep any £, $ or k)
What it means

items.name: Stat · Odometer
items.summary: One number the presenter is talking about, its digits rolling into place like a car’s mileage, with its source.
items.use: When the presenter quotes a figure that deserves a little ceremony: a total, a record, a milestone. Every number carries its source, and it holds long enough to read twice.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The marker scales in and the line draws down (0.90 s) while the wheels spin up from zero and settle from left to right, the right-hand wheels turning most, each with a tiny overshoot (1.20 s, easing out). The label and source fade up as the last wheel settles. Out: the words fade (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What the number is
fields.default: of customers chose the yearly plan

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Stat · Split-flap
items.summary: One number the presenter is talking about, flipping into place like a departures board, with its source.
items.use: When a figure should land like an announcement: results, arrivals, a count that just came in. A short unit (up to three characters, such as % or k) gets flaps of its own. Every number carries its source.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The marker scales in and the line draws down (0.90 s) while the flaps start blank and flip through the characters, stopping from left to right (0.08 s a flip, 1.00 s in all). The label and source fade up as the last flap lands. Out: the words fade (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What the number is
fields.default: of customers chose the yearly plan

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Stat · LED
items.summary: One number the presenter is talking about, lit up on a dot-matrix sign, with its source.
items.use: When a figure should feel like a sign: a score, a countdown, a number that is live in the room. Short figures read best, up to five characters; the sign has digits, % £ $ € k m + - x / and punctuation.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). The marker scales in and the line draws down (0.90 s) while the board powers on with its dark dots (0.20 s) and the figure scrolls in from the right, a column at a time (0.80 s), then blinks once. The label and source fade up. Out: the words fade (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: What the number is
fields.default: of customers chose the yearly plan

fields.label: How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Stat · Live
items.summary: A running total that keeps ticking while the presenter talks, with its source.
items.use: When the number is still moving: sign-ups today, orders this hour, people watching now. It counts up, then goes up by the step you choose every so often while the presenter talks. Say what the count is and where it comes from.
items.motion: The card rises 24 px and fades in (0.40 s). As in W03, the marker scales in, the line draws down (0.90 s) and the number counts up from zero (1.00 s, easing out); the label and source fade up as the count settles. Then it stays live: every 1.5 s or so it goes up, the digits that change rolling into place (0.40 s), and the dot in the Live tag pulses while the card is on screen. Out: the words fade (0.20 s), then the card drops 24 px and fades (0.30 s).

fields.label: How much it goes up each time
How high it sits at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16

items.name: Whip pan
items.summary: A fast pan with motion blur carries scene A out; scene B arrives from the same side and settles.
items.use: Between two scenes when the video moves on quickly: footage to footage, or one idea to the next. Going back runs it the other way; at 9:16 use the Vertical whip (X03), which reads like a scroll.
items.motion: Scene A whips left, speeding up into a horizontal blur (0.25 s, easing in). The cut lands on the frame of heaviest blur, and scene B carries on the same move from the right, slowing and sharpening (0.35 s, easing out). About 0.6 s in all. Sound: a whoosh peaking on the cut.

fields.label: How much blur at the cut

items.name: Vertical whip
items.summary: The same fast whip, up or down, like a hard scroll; natural at 9:16.
items.use: Between two scenes in tall videos for social, where it reads like a scroll: forward moves up, going back moves down.
items.motion: Scene A whips up out of the frame into a vertical blur (0.25 s, easing in); the cut lands on the heaviest blur, and scene B rises in from below and settles (0.35 s, easing out). About 0.6 s in all. Sound: a whoosh on the cut.

fields.label: How much blur at the cut

items.name: Push through
items.summary: The camera pushes into scene A until it passes the lens in a blur, and scene B is behind it.
items.use: Going deeper or moving forward: into a topic, into the product, into the next chapter. Going back the other way, use the Pull back (X05).
items.motion: The camera pushes into scene A, speeding up (0.35 s, easing in), until A fills the lens as a soft blur. The cut hides in that blur, and scene B is already behind it: the camera arrives in B and eases to rest (0.40 s, easing out). About 0.75 s in all. Sound: a low whoosh into the cut.

items.name: Infinite zoom
items.summary: Scene B is hidden in a detail of scene A, and one zoom carries straight into it.
items.use: When scene A shows where B lives: a picture on a wall, a screen in the shot, a window. Plan scene A so the detail is in shot, and give its place in the frame. It reads as going in; going back the other way is the Pull back (X05).
items.motion: A small frame in scene A, here a picture on the wall, already shows scene B. The camera zooms into it in one continuous move (1.00 s, easing in and out, at a steady rate of zoom), so the picture grows until it fills the screen and becomes B. The cut is the moment the picture takes over; the zoom never stops or changes speed there. Sound: a rising whoosh.

fields.label: Where B sits in scene A: left edge (px)
Where B sits in scene A: top edge (px)
Width of that place (px; its height keeps the video’s shape)

items.name: Zoom punch
items.summary: A sharp push-in on the beat; the cut lands at its peak and scene B eases back out.
items.use: To land a big point on a beat of the music: a reveal, a number, the punchline. More than one in a row feels jumpy.
items.motion: On the beat, scene A punches in to about 120% (0.12 s, easing in) with a touch of blur. The cut lands on the peak, so scene B starts at the same zoom and eases back out to 100% (0.38 s, easing out). About 0.5 s in all. Sound: a hit or a kick drum on the cut.

items.name: Speed ramp
items.summary: Scene A speeds away into a smear of blur, and scene B slows out of it into place.
items.use: For energy between two pieces of footage, especially action: travel, sport, a busy day. The footage keeps playing through the ramp.
items.motion: Scene A speeds up from rest to very fast (0.45 s, a steep ease in), smearing into streaks of blur. The cut sits in the smear, and scene B comes out of it fast, then slows to rest (0.40 s, a steep ease out). About 0.85 s in all. Sound: a rising whoosh that drops on landing.

items.name: Corner turn
items.summary: The camera turns 90° in a room of scenes and finds scene B on the next wall.
items.use: Moving on to a new part of the story that sits beside the last: the next room, the next feature, the other side. Turning left goes back.
items.motion: Scenes hang on the walls of a room. The camera turns 90° to the right (0.90 s, easing in and out): scene A slides away round the corner as a wall in perspective, and scene B comes round onto the next wall until it faces the camera. The cut is the moment the corner crosses the middle. Sound: a soft whoosh.

items.name: Parallax slide
items.summary: Both scenes slide across together with a touch of depth, so the move feels deep rather than flat.
items.use: A calm, polished move on to the next scene, footage or animation. It moves both scenes as single layers; for full layered depth, build the scene with the presenter cut out.
items.motion: Both scenes slide left together (0.80 s, easing in and out), scene B settling from slightly larger as scene A eases back a little, so the move feels deep rather than flat. The cut is where the two meet in the middle. Sound: a soft whoosh.

items.name: Rack focus
items.summary: Scene A falls out of focus, and scene B pulls sharp out of the same blur.
items.use: A calm, cinematic change between two pieces of footage: a change of place, time or mood. Sound: none needed, or a soft swell.
items.motion: Scene A falls out of focus (0.40 s, easing in), with a slight breathing push of 2%. The cut hides in the deepest blur, and scene B pulls sharp out of the same blur (0.40 s, easing out). About 0.8 s in all.

items.name: Colour stack
items.summary: Panels in the brand's colours sweep across, each just behind the last; the last one opens on scene B.
items.use: Between any two scenes, footage or animation, when the video moves on to something new. Branded and energetic; it covers any cut.
items.motion: Three panels in the brand's colours sweep in from the left, each 0.06 s behind the last (0.35 s, easing in and out), until the last one, the accent, covers the frame. The cut happens behind it, then the accent panel carries on off to the right and opens on scene B (0.40 s, easing out). About 0.85 s in all. Sound: a layered swish.

items.name: Brand shape
items.summary: A shape from the brand’s mark grows to fill the frame, then opens on scene B.
items.use: Between any two scenes, for a branded moment: the start of a new section, or after the introduction. Pick the brand’s simplest solid shape (or give its own path); a wordmark or a thin outline is too slight to cover the frame.
items.motion: The brand’s shape grows from the middle in the accent colour, faster and faster (0.45 s, easing in), until it covers the frame. The cut happens behind it; then an opening of the same shape grows from the middle (0.55 s, easing out), and scene B shows through it until the colour has gone. About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a soft swell into the cut.

options.label: The brand’s own shape (the path below)

fields.label: The brand’s own shape: an SVG path, drawn in a 100 × 100 box and filling most of it

items.name: Grow from a frame
items.summary: Scene B appears in a small rounded frame that grows until it fills the screen.
items.use: Opening a new idea out of the current scene: a screen, an example, a closer look. The frame can start where the presenter points or gestures (give the point), otherwise it starts in the middle.
items.motion: Scene B appears in a small rounded frame, with a soft shadow (0.15 s, fading in and scaling up from 90%). The frame grows until it fills the screen (0.40 s, easing in and out), moving to the middle as it goes, and its corners ease square as it lands (0.30 s). Scene A stays still underneath. About 0.75 s in all. Sound: a light whoosh.

fields.label: Where the frame starts, across (px from the left; 0 for the middle)
Where the frame starts, down (px from the top; 0 for the middle)

items.name: Parting
items.summary: Scene A splits along a line and the halves slide apart, with scene B underneath.
items.use: Opening up to something new: a reveal, the product, the answer. Put the split where it doesn’t cut through a face; at 9:16 the halves part up and down. For footage, give scene A a second time (the same clip, straight after it) so each half has its own copy.
items.motion: A thin accent line draws down the frame (0.15 s). Scene A splits along it and the two halves slide apart to the sides (0.45 s, easing in), each carrying half of the line on its edge, with scene B already underneath. The cut is the moment B is mostly showing. About 0.6 s in all. Sound: a soft tear or whoosh.

options.label: To the sides, or up and down at 9:16

fields.label: Where it splits (px from the left, or from the top when they part up and down; 0 for the middle)

items.name: Diagonal slice
items.summary: One clean diagonal cut; the two pieces of scene A slide away in opposite directions.
items.use: A sharp, confident move on: a new section, a bold claim, the product. Keep the angle the same in every video, so it becomes part of the brand. For footage, give scene A a second time (the same clip, straight after it) so each piece has its own copy.
items.motion: An accent line slices across scene A on a diagonal (0.10 s). The two pieces slide away from it in opposite directions, and a little along it (0.40 s, easing in), each carrying the line on its edge and revealing scene B underneath. The cut is the moment B is mostly showing. About 0.6 s in all. Sound: a sharp slice.

fields.label: The cut’s angle (degrees from level; negative leans the other way)

items.name: Tile cascade
items.summary: The frame breaks into tiles that turn over in a wave, each with a piece of scene B on the back.
items.use: A playful move on, with some ceremony: into a new section, a reveal, a list of products or people. Best between two calm scenes; at 9:16 the tiles are fewer and larger.
items.motion: Scene A breaks into a grid of tiles as thin gaps open (0.10 s). The tiles turn over in a wave from left to right, each turn 0.25 s and each column a little after the last, showing its piece of scene B on the back. The cut is when half the tiles show B; the gaps close as the last tile lands. About 0.9 s in all. Sound: a ripple of soft clicks.

items.name: Ink spread
items.summary: The brand’s colour spreads like ink to fill the frame, then drains away to scene B.
items.use: Between two scenes in a friendly, organic video: a change of topic, or into the next part of a story. Avoid it for very corporate brands.
items.motion: The brand’s colour blooms from one corner like ink dropped in water, with soft, uneven edges and a drop or two running ahead (0.45 s, easing in), until it fills the frame. The cut happens behind it; then the ink drains away towards the opposite corner, revealing scene B (0.55 s, easing out). About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a soft liquid swell.

fields.label: The corner it spreads from (it drains to the opposite one)

items.name: Line wipe
items.summary: One accent line crosses the frame, and scene B is revealed in its wake.
items.use: A clean, simple move between any two scenes: the next point, the next step. Going back runs it right to left.
items.motion: A single accent line, leaning slightly, crosses the frame from left to right (0.60 s, easing in and out), and scene B is revealed behind it as it passes. The cut is the moment it crosses the middle. About 0.7 s in all. Sound: a clean swipe.

items.name: Shape match
items.summary: A circle in scene A, a button or a dot, becomes the matching circle in scene B.
items.use: When both scenes share a round shape: a play button that becomes a donut chart, a dot that becomes a map pin, a logo that becomes a badge. Give where the circle is in each scene and how big; it lands where B’s own circle builds.
items.motion: A circle in scene A, here a round play button, grows and travels in a gentle arc to where the matching circle sits in scene B (0.40 s, easing in and out), while A fades away behind it and its icon fades. The cut is when it lands on B’s background, with a small settle; then it opens into a ring (0.25 s), and hands over as the rest of B builds round it. About 0.8 s in all. Sound: a soft pop on landing.

fields.label: The circle in A: across (px from the left to its middle; 0 for the stand-in)
The circle in A: down (px from the top to its middle)
The circle in A: its width
The circle in B: across (px from the left to its middle)
The circle in B: down (px from the top to its middle)
The circle in B: its width
How far it opens into a ring once it lands (0 for none)
The mark on the circle in A

items.name: Colour flood
items.summary: Scene A’s main colour floods the frame and becomes scene B’s background.
items.use: When scene A has a strong colour behind it (the presenter on the brand’s colour, a coloured product shot) and scene B is on that same colour: a section title, a statement, the call to action. Use the brand’s colour, or one picked from the footage, and give scene B that background.
items.motion: Scene A’s main colour rises up the frame in a soft wave (0.40 s, easing in) until it covers everything. The cut is that full frame of colour, which simply stays as scene B’s background while the colour layer eases away (0.30 s) and B’s words rise into it. About 0.8 s in all. Sound: a warm swell.

items.name: Card expand
items.summary: A card in scene A opens up to become scene B, like an app opening.
items.use: When scene A shows a card or a widget (a stat, a product tile, a quote) and scene B is the full story behind it: a closer look, the detail, the next screen. Give the card’s place in A, and give B the card’s colour as its background. Reverse it to close back down into the card.
items.motion: The card over scene A lifts, with a soft shadow, and its content fades (0.15 s). It expands to fill the frame (0.40 s, easing in and out), its corners squaring off as it lands, like an app opening from its icon. The cut is when the card fills the screen as scene B’s background; the card layer eases away (0.22 s) and B’s stage and chart build inside it. About 0.8 s in all. Sound: a soft open.

fields.label: The card in A: its left edge (px; 0 for the stand-in)
The card in A: its top edge (px)
The card in A: its width
The card in A: its height

items.name: Shared element
items.summary: A word, logo or product stays on screen and travels to its new place in scene B while everything around it changes.
items.use: When one thing carries over from scene A to scene B: a key word that becomes B’s title, a logo, a product. It must be in both scenes; give where it is in each and how big.
items.motion: One element, here the word “Growth”, stays on screen while everything around it changes: scene A fades to scene B behind it (0.30 s) as the word travels, shrinks and changes colour to its new place as B’s title (0.60 s, easing in and out). The rest of B builds round it as it lands. About 0.9 s in all. Sound: none, or a soft tone on landing.

fields.label: In A: its left edge (px; 0 for the stand-in)

items.name: Line draw
items.summary: A line in scene A, an underline or a rule, runs on across the frame and draws scene B’s layout.
items.use: Into a chart or a diagram: the line under the presenter’s name, or any rule in scene A, becomes the baseline B is built on. Give the line’s place in A and the baseline’s in B; keep the line weight the same as B’s.
items.motion: A line in scene A, here the accent underline under a name, runs on across the frame (0.30 s, easing in) as A fades behind it. It settles as scene B’s baseline (the cut), then draws the rest of B’s layout: the axis rises and the gridlines run out (0.40 s), and B’s chart draws on. About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a light scratch as it runs.

fields.label: The line in A: its left end (px; 0 for the stand-in)
The line in A: its height (px from the top)
The line in A: its length (px)
B’s baseline: its height (px from the top)
The line’s weight (px; 0 for the usual)

items.name: Follow the object
items.summary: Something moving in scene A, a paper plane or the cursor, leads the camera into scene B.
items.use: When an object can carry the story from one scene to the next: a paper plane, the cursor, a ball, a logo. It should belong to the brand or the story. Give where it starts in A and where it lands in B.
items.motion: Something in scene A, here a paper plane, sets off and the camera follows it, panning with motion blur while the plane stays sharp (0.50 s). The cut hides in the blur as the pan carries into scene B, and the plane leads the eye to where B’s story starts, then lands (0.50 s, easing out). About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a whoosh that follows the object.

fields.label: Where it starts in A, across (px; 0 for the stand-in)
Where it starts in A, down (px)
Where it lands in B, across (px)
Where it lands in B, down (px)
How much blur at the cut

items.name: Through the letter
items.summary: Scene B plays inside a giant word that grows until it fills the frame.
items.use: A bold move into a new section or a big idea: the word can name what comes next. Use a short, heavy word; the camera goes through its thickest letter.
items.motion: A word appears over scene A with scene B already playing inside its letters (0.25 s). The word then grows towards the camera, faster and faster (0.75 s), aimed through the thickest part of one letter, until B fills the frame. The cut is when the letters cover the screen; B eases to rest (0.20 s). About 1.2 s in all. Sound: a rising whoosh.

items.name: Word wipe
items.summary: A huge word sweeps across the frame, and the cut happens behind its letters.
items.use: A punchy move on with a word that means something: the next section, the brand’s name, “next”. Use a short word with heavy, upright letters.
items.motion: A word set far bigger than the frame sweeps across it from left to right (0.70 s, easing in and out). Each part of the picture switches from scene A to scene B as a letter passes over it, so the switch always sits behind a letter’s edge and is never seen. About 0.7 s in all. Sound: a heavy whoosh.

fields.label: The word (short, with heavy upright letters)

items.name: Type wall
items.summary: Rows of a repeated word fill the frame, then clear away on scene B.
items.use: A loud, rhythmic move between sections, or into a launch or a call to action. The word can be the brand’s name or the next section’s.
items.motion: Rows of one repeated word, in the brand’s colours, slide in from alternate sides, each row a little after the last (easing out), until they fill the frame at 0.45 s. The cut happens behind the wall; then the rows slide away to the other side, revealing scene B (0.55 s, easing in). About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a rhythmic run of swishes.

items.name: Card stack
items.summary: Scene A shrinks to a card and slides back into a stack; scene B comes forward.
items.use: Moving through chapters or a list, one card after another: steps, examples, case studies. Good for a run of short scenes.
items.motion: Scene A shrinks into a rounded card on the brand’s background (0.25 s, easing out) and slides back and up into a stack of cards, dimming as it goes (0.35 s). Scene B rises from the front of the stack as a card (easing out) and grows to fill the frame (0.30 s, easing in and out). The cut is when B’s card takes the front. About 0.9 s in all. Sound: a soft card shuffle.

items.name: Slide over
items.summary: Scene B slides over scene A with a soft shadow while A sinks back and dims.
items.use: A calm, layered move on: the next step, a new topic, a detail on top of the big picture. Going back slides B off to the right again.
items.motion: Scene B slides in from the right over scene A, casting a soft shadow from its leading edge (0.45 s, easing out), while A scales back to 94% and dims. The cut is when B covers the frame. About 0.7 s in all. Sound: a soft slide.

items.name: Freeze and flick
items.summary: Scene A becomes a photo with a white border and is flicked off the frame.
items.use: A playful move on, from a moment worth keeping: a result, a smile, a before shot. Best on a still moment of footage, as the picture keeps playing inside the photo.
items.motion: Scene A gains a white border and lifts off scene B as a photo, with a flash and a soft shadow (0.15 s). It tilts as if picked up (0.15 s), then is flicked off the top left of the frame (0.30 s, easing in). The cut is the moment it lifts: B plays underneath from then on. About 0.9 s in all. Sound: a camera shutter as it lifts, a flick on the throw.

items.name: Light sweep
items.summary: A soft band of light crosses the frame; the cut hides in its brightest moment.
items.use: Elegant between two pieces of footage, or into a product or a reveal. Quieter than a flash; it suits calm, premium videos.
items.motion: A soft, warm band of light crosses the frame at a slight angle (0.70 s, easing in and out), widening and brightening towards the middle. The cut hides in its brightest frame, when the picture is almost washed out, and the band carries on over scene B and fades. About 0.7 s in all. Sound: a soft shimmer.

items.name: Luma fade
items.summary: Scene B shows first through scene A’s brightest areas, then takes over.
items.use: A soft, cinematic move between two pieces of footage, especially from a bright or contrasty shot. Softer than a crossfade, and it never looks like two pictures stacked.
items.motion: A dissolve that follows the light: scene B appears first through the brightest parts of scene A, then spreads into the mid-tones and finally the shadows (1.00 s, easing in and out). The cut is the halfway point. About 1.0 s in all. Sound: none needed.

fields.label: Scene A’s brightest tone, where B shows first (0 to 1)
Scene A’s darkest tone, where it shows last (0 to 1)

items.name: Halftone
items.summary: Scene A breaks into halftone dots, which resize into scene B.
items.use: A print-like, graphic move: for editorial brands, a magazine feel, or into a chart or a still. Best between two clear pictures.
items.motion: Scene A breaks into a grid of halftone dots, each sized by how dark the picture is there (0.25 s). The dots then shrink away as scene B’s dots grow on the same grid (0.45 s, easing in and out), and B resolves out of them (0.30 s). The cut is the halfway point of the resize. About 1.0 s in all. Sound: a soft crackle.

items.name: Glitch
items.summary: Four frames of digital break-up, with split colour and offset slices, for tech brands. Never longer.
items.use: Only for tech brands, and only at a real change of topic. Use it once or twice in a video at most.
items.motion: Four frames, no more (about 0.17 s): scene A breaks into offset horizontal slices with its colours split into the accent and a cool grey; the middle frames mix slices of A and B; the last lands clean on scene B. The cut sits in the middle frame. Sound: a short digital crackle.

items.name: Stutter cut
items.summary: Two quick flashes between the scenes on the beat, then it lands on scene B.
items.use: On a strong beat in the music: energetic videos, launches, social. Needs a clear beat; without one it looks like a mistake. Start it on the beat.
items.motion: On the beat, the edit flicks to scene B for two frames, back to scene A for two, then lands on B with a small 4% punch that eases out (0.25 s). The final cut is the landing. About 0.5 s in all. Sound: hits on each flash, in time with the music.

fields.label: Each flash (two frames at 24 fps is 0.083 s)
How far B pushes in as it lands (1.04 is 4%)

items.name: Cursor click
items.summary: The cursor clicks a button and scene B opens out of it.
items.use: In a screen recording or a product demo: the viewer sees the click that leads to the next screen. Use the button the viewer would really press, and give its place in scene A.
items.motion: The cursor glides to a button and clicks it: the cursor dips and an accent ring pulses round the button (0.15 s). Scene B then opens out of the button’s shape, growing to fill the frame (0.45 s, easing in and out). The cut is when B covers the screen. About 0.8 s in all. Sound: a click, then a soft whoosh.

fields.label: The button: its left edge (px; 0 for the stand-in)

items.name: Scroll
items.summary: The page scrolls on, and scene B is further down it.
items.use: When both scenes are parts of one page: a website, an app, a long document. Natural for websites and at 9:16.
items.motion: Scene A is the top of a page; scene B is further down the same page. The page scrolls (0.80 s, easing in and out) with a touch of vertical motion blur at its fastest, and a scrollbar moves with it, until B is in place. The cut is the halfway point. About 0.8 s in all. Sound: a soft scroll tick.

items.name: Swipe
items.summary: A phone swipe: scene B slides in like the next story.
items.use: Made for 9:16: stories, reels and anything that should feel like a phone. Going back swipes the other way.
items.motion: Like swiping to the next story: a touch appears, scene A is dragged left with rounded corners and a slight scale-down, and scene B follows it in from the right (0.45 s, easing out after the drag). The story bar at the top moves on to the next segment. The cut is when B passes the middle. About 0.6 s in all. Sound: a soft swipe.

items.name: Notification takeover
items.summary: A notification drops in and expands to become scene B.
items.use: When the next scene is news to the viewer: a result, a message, an alert, the product telling you something. The app name and words should match the story.
items.motion: A notification drops in from the top of scene A with a soft shadow (0.20 s, easing out). It then expands, its contents giving way to scene B (0.45 s, easing in and out), until it fills the frame. The cut is when it covers the screen. About 1.0 s in all. Sound: the notification chime, then a soft whoosh.
